canonical_hits.stem: A Massachusetts LTC facility has 120 licensed beds, so its Schedule II-V analgesic emergency-kit category is capped at 75 units. Which proposed analgesic configurations stay within that category cap? Select all that apply.

choices.text: 40 morphine units plus 35 hydromorphone units
20 morphine, 20 oxycodone, and 20 hydromorphone units
76 oxycodone units
45 morphine units plus 31 oxycodone units
25 morphine units plus 25 oxycodone units

canonical_hits.stem: A pharmacy will place an acute-use ADD inside a Massachusetts inpatient hospice. Which requirements are part of the current hospice pathway? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Continuously monitor the ADD by video
Keep medications in the hospice ADD as pharmacy property until they are dispensed.
Skip prescription reconciliation because the medications are palliative
Obtain a machine-specific Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration
Determine whether a machine-specific DEA registration is required

canonical_hits.stem: A Massachusetts inpatient hospice has 18 licensed beds. What is the maximum number of Schedule II-V analgesic units permitted in its acute-use ADD under the current circular?

choices.text: A maximum stock of 40 analgesic units
A maximum stock of 60 analgesic units
A maximum stock of 75 analgesic units
A maximum stock of 100 analgesic units
A maximum stock of 150 analgesic units

canonical_hits.stem: An inpatient Massachusetts hospice has 18 licensed beds. Under the acute-use ADD circular, its caps are 100 Schedule II-V analgesic units, 60 Schedule II-V sedative/anticonvulsant units, and 50 Schedule VI ancillary units. Which proposed category totals comply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: 101 Schedule II-V analgesic units because one extra unit may be borrowed from the ancillary category
70 Schedule II-V sedative units because the hospice has fewer than 21 beds
100 units of approved morphine/other Schedule II-V analgesic stock in the analgesic category
60 units of approved lorazepam/other Schedule II-V sedative stock in the sedative category
40 units of an approved Schedule VI ancillary antiemetic in the ancillary category

canonical_hits.stem: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy uses one ADD only as an approved emergency medication kit and a second ADD for routine medication dispensing. A licensed nurse asks to load both machines. Which answer best applies under the current ADD policy?

choices.text: The nurse may load the emergency-kit ADD; routine-dispensing ADD loading is limited to certified technicians or interns under pharmacist supervision.
The nurse may load both machines because the same pharmacy owns both devices and supervises the medication inventory.
The nurse may load neither machine because routine and emergency ADDs are restricted to pharmacists and pharmacy interns.
The nurse may load the routine machine whenever it contains only Schedule VI medications and no federally controlled drugs.
Both machines use the emergency-kit loader list as long as they are located inside the same Massachusetts retail pharmacy.

canonical_hits.stem: A Massachusetts long-term-care facility is building its controlled-substance emergency-kit formulary with its single pharmacy provider. The facility wants to include a controlled analgesic. Which framework applies?

choices.text: Any quantity is allowed if the drug is Schedule VI.
The facility selects from approved Schedule II-V analgesic choices within the bed-capacity unit limit.
Only Schedule II analgesics may be included.
Controlled analgesics are prohibited from LTC emergency kits.
The pharmacy may ignore facility policies once DPH approves the drug class.

canonical_hits.stem: An inpatient Massachusetts hospice asks its pharmacy provider to keep a large non-patient-specific supply of acute-use controlled medications in the onsite ADD so the facility can avoid routine pharmacy deliveries. Which statement best describes the permitted acute-use purpose?

choices.text: It is a limited bridge for timely palliation until the pharmacy can fill and deliver the full patient prescription.
It is intended to reduce routine pharmacy deliveries by functioning as standing floor stock for chronic therapy.
It is intended primarily to hold larger reserve quantities when the hospice has frequent Schedule VI use.
It is intended mainly for resuscitation drugs used during immediately life-threatening emergencies.
It transfers ordinary dispensing responsibility from the pharmacy to hospice nursing staff during off-hours.

canonical_hits.stem: A Massachusetts inpatient hospice uses its acute-use ADD for morphine, lorazepam, and approved Schedule VI ancillary medications. Which actions fit the purpose and accountability of this program? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Dispense untracked Schedule VI ancillary doses because they are outside federal Schedules II-V
Use an acute morphine dose for timely palliation while the pharmacy prepares and delivers the patient's full prescription
Reconcile a lorazepam dose removed from the ADD with the patient's prescription/order
Keep the ADD contents as pharmacy property until doses are dispensed for administration
Use the cabinet to avoid filling routine long-term prescriptions whenever delivery is inconvenient

canonical_hits.stem: Which statements correctly describe Massachusetts LTC emergency-kit safeguards? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Each Schedule II-V unit should be tamper-evident/resistant and individually packaged as a single dose
A facility may use an ADD instead of the traditional locked box when relevant requirements are met
Schedule VI emergency doses remain subject to procurement, storage, dispensing, administration, recording, and disposal controls
Schedule VI emergency stock is exempt from the facility quality-assurance process
Once a kit is approved, controlled-substance accountability policies are optional

canonical_hits.stem: A Massachusetts LTC facility has 120 licensed beds, giving its Schedule II-V sedative/anticonvulsant emergency-kit category a 25-unit cap. Which configurations stay within that cap? Select all that apply.

choices.text: 5 lorazepam, 5 alprazolam, and 5 pregabalin units
26 lorazepam units
15 alprazolam units plus 15 pregabalin units
10 lorazepam units plus 10 alprazolam units
25 pregabalin units

canonical_hits.stem: A Massachusetts LTC facility has 120 licensed beds. It wants its emergency kit to contain the maximum allowed number of Schedule II-V analgesic units. What is the current maximum for that analgesic category?

choices.text: 45 units
60 units
75 units
90 units
120 units

canonical_hits.stem: A retail pharmacy plans to use an ADD for routine medication dispensing rather than only as an emergency kit. Which controls apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Have it loaded by a certified pharmacy technician or pharmacy intern under Massachusetts pharmacist supervision
Maintain transaction and reconciliation records for the routine ADD program.
Treat the machine as exempt from pharmacy policies because it is computer controlled
Obtain a machine-specific DEA registration and Controlled Substance Registration as required by the policy
Continuously monitor the ADD by video
